title: OpenTelemetry-compatible traces with declared span attributes
asA: on-call engineer following a slow request across services
iWant: a span per request carrying auth class, resource id, and response status, linked to downstream spans
soThat: latency and failure are attributable to a hop, not to the system in general

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every handled request produces an OpenTelemetry-compatible server span named by method and path template, with correct start, end, and status.
acceptanceCriteria.then: a server span exists with the method and path template name and timing that brackets the request

acceptanceCriteria.description: Spans carry the declared attributes: auth class, resource id where the route binds one, response status code, and the request id.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a request to a resource endpoint
acceptanceCriteria.then: auth class, resource id, status code, and request id are present

acceptanceCriteria.description: Inbound trace context (traceparent) is honoured: the server span joins the caller's trace rather than starting a fresh one.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a request carrying a valid traceparent header
acceptanceCriteria.then: it carries the inbound trace id as its parent context

acceptanceCriteria.description: Downstream calls made on behalf of a request (database, cache, HTTP) produce child spans within the request's trace with the trace context propagated onward.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a request whose handler calls a downstream dependency
acceptanceCriteria.then: the downstream call appears as a child span and the dependency received the propagated context

acceptanceCriteria.description: Error responses mark their span status as error with the problem type recorded, so failed requests are findable by span status alone.
acceptanceCriteria.then: span status is error and the problem type is recorded as an attribute
